takeaways: Humana's adjusted loss of 70 cents a share beat the $1.00 loss Wall Street expected, and revenue of $41.16 billion topped the $40.87 billion consensus (Investing.com).
On a GAAP basis the company earned $1.33 a share, lifted by put/call valuation gains on minority investments; adjusted pretax profit was much thinner after stripping those items.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance moved to 'at least $9.50' from 'at least $9.00,' above the $9.16 Street number Investing.com cites; GAAP EPS guidance jumped to at least $15.09 from $6.52.
The insurance segment's GAAP benefit ratio came in at 93.7%, better than management's 'slightly above 94%' guide — medical costs ran a bit cooler than feared.
CenterWell Senior Primary Care patients are up 146,800 year to date (+30%), and Medicaid membership is up 103,600 (+7%) on Duals programs in Michigan, Illinois and South Carolina.
verdict: Losing 70 cents instead of a buck is somehow a win in Medicare Advantage land, and Humana stacked a guidance raise on top. Medical costs behaved, CenterWell keeps adding patients, and the Street got the raise it was already half-expecting. Max's take: not a fireworks quarter — more like a quietly competent one that still left the stock a little soft premarket.

sources.title: Investing.com: Humana beats estimates, raises guidance
